top_level.ADVISORY_BODY: The tape keeps grinding to new highs: the Nasdaq Composite closed Monday at a record 27,477.31 (+1.05%), its 23rd record close of 2026, with the S&P 500 (+0.66%) and Dow (+0.18% to 51,267.90) both green and Nasdaq 100 futures still pushing higher into this morning's open on Nvidia's continued run (premarket +2%, market value approaching $6 trillion after Monday's close at an all-time-high $239.11). The nuance the headline misses: Monday's advance was narrow. Only 1,566 of 3,035 Nasdaq issues (50.6%) actually rose, a 1.07:1 advance/decline ratio against a 1.93:1 volume ratio — megacaps (NVDA +2.12%, MSFT +1.48%) did the work while most constituents lagged or fell, the same concentration risk this pipeline has flagged before. The macro backdrop is genuinely easing: the 10-Year Treasury yield, which touched 5.34% intraday Monday (a fresh 2002-era, 24-year high), has pulled back to roughly 5.26-5.27% this morning, and WTI crude has slid to roughly $87.65-88.41 (Brent just under $100 for the first time in weeks) as the G7's planned 100-million-barrel reserve release over the next four months and improving Middle East export volumes work through the market — even as Iran escalates, not de-escalates, its campaign of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz (nearly 20 commercial ships hit over the past month, per Benzinga) and insists Hormuz stays constrained until Washington meets seven conditions. Kalshi's implied odds of an October 28 Fed hike have bounced between roughly 16% (right after Friday's weak jobs miss) and roughly 25% this morning, still solidly pricing a hold. The one operational note that matters most for today's futures-level work: Schwab's /ES and /NQ data feed failed with an HTTP 400 error on every attempt during this morning's data pull, and the FMP cash-index fallback did not populate either contract either — there are no real settlement, pivot, or value-area numbers for /ES or /NQ today, and the Analysis/Trade Idea/Levels boxes below say so plainly rather than inventing any. Trade the cash-index and single-name setups below; treat today's /ES and /NQ cards as informational only until the feed is restored.

top_level.CA_ROTATION: Monday's NASDAQ sector snapshot (FMP, 10/5 close) shows the broadening the index-level record doesn't: Industrials led by a wide margin (+4.04%), with Utilities (+2.14%), Consumer Cyclical (+1.66%) and Communication Services (+1.64%) also strong — a genuine rotation into rate-sensitive and cyclical names as the 10Y eased off its 2002-era high. Technology, the sector actually carrying the Nasdaq Composite's headline gain (NVDA, MSFT), posted just +0.39%, the second-weakest NASDAQ sector read — the same megacap-vs-breadth divergence flagged above. Real Estate was the lone red sector (-0.15%), a mild drag despite falling yields. RAMP read: the AI/Quantum sleeve's headline strength (NVDA near $6T) isn't matched by the broader Technology sector snapshot, reinforcing that this is a concentration story, not sector-wide confirmation; Blockchain sleeve (BTC +0.38%, ETH +0.09%, our feed) is quiet, sitting out both the rates-relief and oil-relief stories.
